messages:
sarah.h: Quick heads-up — ACME deal POC: traces aren’t showing up in Datadog dashboards after we enabled the log-forwarder. Can anyone help triage?
omar.k: I can take a look. Are we seeing 429s or dropped events on our side?
sarah.h: Datadog says accepted, but link tracing between frontend -> gateway -> inference is broken. Missing trace_id in the forwarded logs.
lee: Most likely header rewrite at the gateway. Do we have the request_id/traceparent preserved?
maria_p: Client app sets X-Request-Id, but the nginx proxy we deployed for them strips unknown headers by default.
tomas: If headers are stripped, Datadog will show separate spans. Quick fix: enable proxy pass-through for trace headers. In nginx: 
```
proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $http_x_request_id;
proxy_set_header traceparent $http_traceparent;
```
omar.k: Also confirm our log formatter includes trace_id field. For our side (inference) we emit `trace_id` as `trace.id` in JSON — Datadog mapping expects `dd.trace_id` sometimes. Could be a mapping mismatch.
sarah.h: Ugh, customer is on a tight timeline. Can we patch config remotely or do they need a redeploy?
lee: If it's just nginx config we can remote into their bastion and update, no redeploy. But they block egress to external endpoints — need to confirm allowed IPs for log drain.
maria_p: Sales asked about export endpoints and firewall rules earlier. @tomas do we have the outbound IP range for our log forwarder and trace egress?
tomas: Yes — forwarding IPs are 18.200.34.0/24 and 52.11.77.0/24 for the region they use. Also TCP 443 to logs.datadoghq.com. I'll paste the list to the ticket.
ops-bot: Incident 5421 created: "ACME POC trace missing in Datadog" — assignees: omar.k, lee.
omar.k: While we patch proxy, we should also check batching: their client is sending very bursty requests and we hit our rate cap on the log exporter, which can 429 and silently drop events. Check exporter logs for backoff/retry.
sarah.h: How do we surface 429 backoffs to the customer? They only see gaps in the UI.
lee: We can enable the forwarder debug logs (temporarily) and expose a sample `curl` to reproduce. Example: 
```
curl -X POST https://our-forwarder.example.com/ingest -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"trace_id":"abc123","msg":"test"}'
```
maria_p: Also confirm token/scoping — the token they used had ingestion-only scope but not trace-linking scope. Mistmatch can accept logs but not attach to traces. @sarah.h can you confirm token id in their settings?
sarah.h: Token is prod-ingest-ACME-01. I’ll DM the token to infra for verification.
tomas: If token scopes are the issue we can re-issue a scope-correct token. But first two actions: 1) enable header passthrough on customer nginx, 2) temporarily enable forwarder debug and monitoring to catch 429s.
omar.k: I’ve found exporter logs — exponential backoff kicking in around 13:02 UTC, 429 repeated for ~45s, then resumed. I’ll attach snippet to the incident.
lee: For longer term, recommend: enforce `traceparent` and `tracestate` passthrough, add a sample dashboard widget that correlates `trace_id` count with `log.accepted` to detect gaps automatically. I can draft the dashboard JSON.
maria_p: Sales note — customer asked whether we can send logs to Splunk instead of Datadog. Any blocker?
tomas: Splunk works but requires different field mapping and a HEC token. Also need to confirm whether they want raw log drain or processed events; processed keeps us enrichers.
sarah.h: Customer is okay with Datadog if we can prove end-to-end traces within 24h. Can we commit?
omar.k: Yes — if infra approves remote config change and we throttle/export retries tuned we should be good.
lee: I’ll prepare the nginx patch and a short runbook for their ops with exact firewall entries and the curl tests.
ops-bot: Reminder: deploy window approval required for remote changes — please add change request to the incident.
sarah.h: Thanks team — I’ll update the customer and loop back once runbook is ready. :thumbsup:
omar.k: Ping me when ready, I’ll validate in Datadog.
lee: Will post the dashboard JSON in the incident.
maria_p: I’ll hold the pricing question aside — if they need custom log retention or a dedicated exporter we’ll quote separately.
sarah.h: Closing the loop — next update by EOD PST.
